competencies.name: DNS zone and record-set reconnaissance
competencies.produces: zone record set (NS/SOA/MX/TXT/SRV), nameserver inventory, resolved-name-to-address map, zone-transfer vs closed-zone verdict
inputs_required: registrable domain or a nameserver address
declared SOA secondary set for the expectation baseline
competencies.contact_rationale: Depth is only demonstrable against a live authoritative server. A refused AXFR and a stale-serial replica differ only in the wire response, so published RFC text alone cannot separate them. Assessable from captured tool output, never by scanning.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher (IETF RFC for the transfer semantics, plus a second independent org for the expectation baseline) AND a disproof clause that names the observable which would refute it (stale SOA serial, or success from an address outside the declared secondary set)

coverage.justification: measured: tools/recon_audit_offtopic.py reports 14/22 off-topic (63.6%) for dns_enum, plus 4 module-filler items. The generated projection domains/network/infrastructure/dns_enum/skills/SKILL.md renders XSS, SQLi, buffer-overflow and Hack-The-Box module blurbs as dns_enum techniques. 3 of the 8 on-topic items carry real, high-quality validation and FP logic; the class is repairable, not empty. fp_cases=0 measured from the fp_case table, despite wks.cli gaps printing an 'fp' column of 2 (that column counts fp_rule items, not fp_case rows).

competencies.name: Passive subdomain and hostname discovery
competencies.produces: passive hostname set with per-name provenance (which public source yielded it) and a resolve-or-not flag
competencies.contact_rationale: Studyable entirely from published material and from archived/captured passive-DNS output. The name comes from a public log, not from the target. Fully assessable without contacting the target; live resolution is a separate, contact-requiring competency.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher describing the log's publication guarantee (IETF for CT log semantics) plus a second independent org, AND a disproof that names what separates a real passive finding from a wildcard-DNS artifact

coverage.justification: measured: no bug_class covers passive name discovery. The only dns_enum item that mentions certificate transparency (1 of 1111 active items) is about AXFR refusal, not CT logs. recon_audit_offtopic.py returns no verdict for a passive class because none exists to probe.

competencies.name: Reachable service discovery and port inventory
competencies.produces: port-to-service inventory per host, with open/filtered/closed tri-state and the probe that produced each state
competencies.contact_rationale: open vs filtered is a firewall behaviour observable only in the response pattern. Not derivable from documentation. Assessable only from captured scan output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher (IETF for the service/transport registry, second org for state semantics) plus a disproof naming the observable that distinguishes a real listener from a rate-limit artifact

coverage.justification: measured: service_enumeration 10/14 off-topic (71.4%), exposed_services 13/21 off-topic (61.9%), 6 module-filler. Combined 23/35 off-topic. Both classes are vocabulary-matched to this competency, so the topicality failure is in the item text, not the class definition.

competencies.name: Service configuration and version fingerprinting
competencies.produces: per-service configuration profile: version, enabled features, anonymous or default access posture, credential policy
competencies.contact_rationale: A banner is a fact about a running instance. Version inference from a handshake is a reasoning step over captured bytes. Not studyable from published prose alone.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher documenting the specific configuration default being claimed, plus a disproof naming the version or build whose behaviour would differ

coverage.justification: measured: service_enumeration_detail 11/16 off-topic (68.8%), service_enumeration 10/14 off-topic (71.4%). 21/30 off-topic. The class page itself advertises 'protocol configuration as the root cause behind the rest', which is the right intent, but the items do not execute it.

competencies.name: Remote management and administration surface discovery
competencies.produces: inventory of RMM agents, admin panels, VNC/RDP/SMB/WinRM consoles reachable from the assessment position, each with the policy that should have blocked it
competencies.contact_rationale: Whether a management plane is reachable from a given source is a network-path fact. Studyable in principle, demonstrable only against a captured path or a topology model.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher stating the vendor's own reachability guidance, plus a disproof naming the network control whose presence would make reachability an accepted condition rather than a finding

coverage.justification: measured: tools/recon_audit_offtopic.py reports 19/23 off-topic (82.6%) for exposed_rmm, the worst ratio of any probed class. 4 on-topic items remain. This class cannot currently be assessed as RMM discovery knowledge.

competencies.name: Internal endpoint and host discovery
competencies.produces: live host list per subnet with the discovery mechanism that found each host (ARP, NBNS, ICMP, DNS) and the subnet/segment it belongs to
inputs_required: subnet list or a positioned host
competencies.contact_rationale: Liveness is a response. Silent-drop segmentation makes a negative result indistinguishable from a dead host without a second probe, which is exactly the reasoning the assessment must exercise on captured output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher on the discovery mechanism's semantics, plus a disproof naming the artefact that would show a discovered host is not really a host (a proxy, a NAT boundary, a wildcard responder)

coverage.justification: measured: 7/12 off-topic (58.3%). Below MATURITY_MIN_ITEMS=12 it sits exactly on the boundary, so 5 usable items cannot reach mature even if they were all on-topic.

competencies.name: Segmentation and reachable-path analysis
competencies.produces: segment map with the enforced boundaries, the paths that were confirmed to cross them, and the controls that would explain a blocked path
competencies.contact_rationale: A segmentation claim is a claim about which paths were attempted and which answered. Architecture reasoning over a hypothetical topology is possible, but the disproof (a control that should have blocked the observed path) is only checkable against a real topology.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher describing the boundary control's enforcement point, plus a disproof naming the configuration that would have permitted the crossing

coverage.justification: measured: 13/20 off-topic (65.0%), 2 module-filler. Also one of the 9 NETWORK classes flagged in CONTROL/OPERATOR.md as historically seeded on mitre.org alone; its current seed set now spans microsoft.com + mitre.org + rfc-editor.org per wks.network_taxonomy._NET_SEED, so the promotion blocker is resolved but the topicality defect is not.

competencies.name: Active Directory domain and object enumeration
competencies.produces: domain/forest object record set: DCs, trusts, users, groups, computers, SPNs, GPO links, with the LDAP filter that returned each
inputs_required: domain controller hostname or LDAP base DN
competencies.contact_rationale: The enumerable set is a function of the directory's ACLs and the bind context in use. Published AD schema tells you what COULD be listed, never what IS listable here. Requires contact, but assessable on captured LDAP output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher (Microsoft Open Specifications for the LDAP semantics, second independent org for the enumeration consequence) plus a disproof naming the filter or ACL state that would make the record set legitimately smaller

coverage.justification: measured: 12/22 off-topic (54.5%), 6 module-filler. Also named in CONTROL/OPERATOR.md as one of the 9 network classes that could never promote; seed set is now mitre.org + rfc-editor.org (2 orgs), so that blocker is resolved. Topicality is not.

competencies.name: LDAP service and directory-structure reconnaissance
competencies.produces: directory tree structure, rootDSE attributes, naming contexts, supported LDAP controls and extensions, anonymous-bind verdict per context
competencies.contact_rationale: rootDSE content and supportedControls are per-instance facts. RFC 4511 defines the shape; the instance decides the contents. Requires contact, assessable on captured output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the IETF LDAP specification for the protocol semantics plus a second independent org for the exposure consequence, and a disproof naming the control or ACL that would restrict the read

coverage.justification: measured: ad_ldap is 0/21 off-topic and is the one clean recon-adjacent class in the tree. ldap_enum is 8/16 off-topic (50.0%). The competency as a whole is salvageable: ad_ldap's 21 items can carry it once ldap_enum is either repaired or demoted to a pointer stub under R14.

competencies.name: AD trust, SPN and replication-topology discovery
competencies.produces: trust edge list with directionality and transitivity, SPN-to-account map, DC replication topology, delegation flag per affected principal
inputs_required: AD object record set from internal_ad_enumeration
competencies.contact_rationale: Trust directionality and delegation flags are directory state. Their security consequence is documented, but the graph itself is only observable from a live directory. Assessable on captured record sets.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from Microsoft Open Specifications for the trust or delegation semantics plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the trust attribute value that would make the edge a one-way, non-transitive, already-filtered path

coverage.justification: measured: ad_trust_abuse 14/14 on-topic, ad_kerberos 13/13 on-topic, 0 off-topic between them. 1 fp_case row across the pair, both classes chained (ad-delegation-replay-to-dcsync-domain-admin, constrained-delegation-to-admin-service-ticket, ad-enum-to-kerberoast-to-lateral-execution, spn-enumeration-to-offline-service-hash-crack). These are the only two NETWORK classes that are topically clean.

competencies.name: Group Policy object and link discovery
competencies.produces: GPO inventory with SYSVOL link path, applied-to list per OU, and the specific right that makes each GPO writable or delegable
competencies.contact_rationale: Link paths and applied-to sets are directory state, not documentation. Requires contact; assessable on captured LDAP output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from Microsoft documentation for the GPO application semantics plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the link order or enforced state that would block the write path

coverage.justification: measured: 13/13 on-topic, 0 off-topic. Meets MATURITY_MIN_ITEMS=12. Weakest point: fp_cases=0, which OPERATOR.md cycle priority ranks as the highest-value gap of all three.

competencies.name: SMB share, session and dialect reconnaissance
competencies.produces: share list with ACLs, supported dialect range, signing requirement, null/guest session verdict per host
competencies.contact_rationale: Dialect negotiation and signing requirement are negotiated at connection time. Not studyable from documentation.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the IETF SMB specification for the dialect and signing semantics plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the dialect or signing state that would refute the exposure

coverage.justification: measured: 6/13 off-topic (46.2%), 2 module-filler. smb has the widest publisher spread of any recon class (11 hosts / 11 orgs including rfc-editor.org, specterops.io, rapid7.com, tenable.com, mollysec.com), so the contamination is an item-selection failure, not a sourcing failure.

competencies.name: RDP service exposure and NLA assessment
competencies.produces: per-host RDP posture: NLA enforced or absent, CredSSP/negotiation result, session and channel surface
competencies.contact_rationale: NLA enforcement is a server-side policy observable in the negotiation exchange. Requires contact; assessable on captured handshakes.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from Microsoft Open Specifications for the negotiation semantics plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the negotiation result that would show NLA is enforced

coverage.justification: measured: 15/15 on-topic, 0 off-topic, 15 items clears MATURITY_MIN_ITEMS=12. 2 named chains (rdp-valid-account-to-clipboard-exfiltration, reachable-admin-service-to-relayed-credential-to-lateral). Gap: fp_cases=0.

competencies.name: WinRM/WSMan service exposure assessment
competencies.produces: per-host WinRM posture: listener on 5985 vs 5986, authentication mode, PSRemoting constraint state
competencies.contact_rationale: Listener presence and auth mode are endpoint configuration, observable only by connecting. Requires contact; assessable on captured output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from Microsoft documentation for the WSMan listener and auth-mode semantics plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the auth mode that would refute the exposure

coverage.justification: measured: 13/15 on-topic, 2/15 off-topic (13.3%) - the mildest contamination of any NETWORK recon class, and the only one under 20% off-topic. fp_cases=0. Seed spans microsoft.com + mitre.org (2 orgs).

competencies.name: GraphQL schema and operation discovery
competencies.produces: full type graph, operation and field inventory, resolver-side object reach set, introspection-enabled verdict
competencies.contact_rationale: Introspection is a query against the running schema. Depth is reasoning over the returned type graph, which is a captured artifact. Requires contact to obtain; assessable without.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher (OWASP GraphQL Cheat Sheet) plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the schema element that would make the finding a non-finding (a type not reachable from any query root)

coverage.justification: measured: 13/13 on-topic, 0 off-topic. Strongest recon-supporting class in the corpus: 3 fp_case rows (the most of any class besides sqli/ssrf/jwt/xss) and a named chain graphql-exposure-to-enumeration.

competencies.name: Dangling-record and subdomain takeover validation
competencies.produces: per-name claimability verdict: dangling CNAME/NS/MX/A record, the de-provisioned provider fingerprint that answered, and the claim precondition
inputs_required: name set from subdomain_discovery or dns_zone_recon
the vendor fingerprint that answered on the orphaned name
competencies.contact_rationale: Claimability is proven by the provider's own not-provisioned response on the orphaned name. That response is a contact. Assessment is a decision-sequencing exercise over the observed fingerprint and the record type.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher (OWASP or IETF for the record semantics) plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the record state that would make the name NOT claimable (an active TXT/ACM challenge, or a provider that re-issues on demand)

coverage.justification: measured: 14/14 on-topic, 0 off-topic. Note the dependency defect: this class is clean but its upstream input, subdomain_discovery, is ABSENT. The class's own competency docs assume certificate-transparency and archive sources that do not exist in the corpus. 2 named chains (dangling-dns-to-session-cookie-theft, dangling-ns-to-transitive-zone-compromise, dns-zone-transfer-to-subdomain-takeover).

competencies.name: Web application and entry-point discovery
competencies.produces: application inventory per host: distinct apps behind a shared IP, login surfaces, admin surfaces, API prefixes
competencies.contact_rationale: Which apps sit behind an IP is a fact about the current deployment. Requires contact to observe; assessable on captured HTTP response sets.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher on virtual hosting or app-separation semantics plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the shared-header evidence that would prove two paths are the same app

coverage.justification: measured: no bug_class performs application discovery. The 41 items in open_redirect and the 70 in xss are about the flaw, not about finding the app. db substring probe for 'endpoint discovery' returns 0 items.

competencies.name: Technology stack and component fingerprinting
competencies.produces: component set: web server, framework, CMS, application platform, client-side libraries, with the evidence value that identified each and a confidence tier
competencies.contact_rationale: Headers, asset names and error shapes are runtime observations. Published fingerprint databases document what a value MEANS, never what a given target emits. Requires contact; assessable on captured responses.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher (W3C for the header/asset semantics, OWASP for the disclosure consequence) plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the shared-hosting or proxy layer that would make the header untrustworthy as a stack indicator

coverage.justification: measured: NO class performs fingerprinting. The adjacent class info_disclosure has 15 items (9 on-topic, 6 off-topic, 40%) but its observable is a disclosure, not a stack inference; it cannot carry this competency. The database's own dns_enum page cites the 'Server' header as a fingerprint risk while no class teaches how to read one. This is the largest single hole on the web side of the registry.

competencies.name: Virtual host and Host-header surface discovery
competencies.produces: vhost set per IP with the Host value that produced a distinct response, including default-server and catch-all verdicts
competencies.contact_rationale: A vhost is distinguished from the default only by a differential response. That is a contact by definition. Assessment is a differential-response reasoning exercise on captured output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the IETF HTTP specification for the Host-header routing semantics plus a second independent org (a web-server project's own documentation), and a disproof naming the byte-identical response that would prove the candidate is the catch-all default

coverage.justification: measured: NO class performs vhost discovery. db substring probe for 'virtual host' and 'vhost' both return 0 items across 1111 active items. The adjacent host_header class (12 items, 12 on-topic) is about host-header POISONING, a different observable with a different disproof; it is topically clean but cannot carry enumeration.

competencies.name: Content, path and file discovery
competencies.produces: discovered path set with status/size/word-class fingerprints for each, plus the false-positive discrimination (200-with-soft-404 vs real content)
competencies.contact_rationale: A path is discovered by a differential HTTP response. The hard part of this competency is precisely that discrimination, which lives in the response. Requires contact; assessable on captured status/size distributions.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from OWASP Web Security Testing Guide on content discovery plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the soft-404 signature (constant length, or a redirect to a login page) that would make a 200 a non-finding

coverage.justification: measured: NO class performs content discovery. db substring probe for 'content discovery' returns 0 items. The nearest material is path_traversal (33 items, all on-topic) which concerns traversal of a KNOWN path, not discovery of unknown ones.

competencies.name: Parameter and field discovery
competencies.produces: parameter inventory per endpoint with source (declared, inferred, observed in traffic), type, and the injection relevance tier
competencies.contact_rationale: Undocumented parameters are established by differential request/response pairs or by static analysis of shipped bundles. Requires contact to confirm; the bundle-analysis half is assessable from captured artifacts.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the OpenAPI specification for parameter definition semantics plus OWASP for the mass-assignment consequence, and a disproof naming the ignored-or-echoed parameter that would make a discovered field inert

coverage.justification: measured: NO class performs parameter discovery. db substring probe for 'parameter discovery' returns 0 items. mass_assign (14 items, all on-topic) and nosql (16, all on-topic) describe the flaw that over-posting enables, not the enumeration of the parameter set.

competencies.name: API endpoint and version discovery
competencies.produces: endpoint inventory with method, auth scheme, and version, including the machine-readable description when one is published
competencies.contact_rationale: Endpoints are enumerated by probing candidate paths or by extracting them from shipped client artifacts. Probing is contact; client-artifact extraction is not, but the confirmation step is.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the OpenAPI Initiative specification for the description format plus OWASP API Security Top 10 for the exposure consequence, and a disproof naming the version the endpoint belongs to that would be out of scope

coverage.justification: measured: NO class performs API endpoint discovery. The adjacent api_trust class (14 items, 14 on-topic, 0 off-topic) addresses trust boundaries BETWEEN already-known endpoints. The web tree's areas/api/ directories (rest, graphql, websocket, other) are organisational folders, not discovery competencies, and carry no items of their own.

competencies.name: Certificate and TLS configuration intelligence
competencies.produces: certificate chain inventory with SAN set, issuer, validity window and CT-log presence, plus TLS parameter posture per endpoint
competencies.contact_rationale: Certificate data is published in CT logs and is quotable without touching the target. The SAN set is the single highest-yield passive asset source in all of recon. Fully assessable from published material and archived CT output; live handshake inspection is a separate, contact-requiring competency and is deliberately NOT what this competency claims.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the IETF Certificate Transparency specification (RFC 6962) for the log guarantee, plus a second independent org from the CA/Browser Forum for the issuance requirement, and a disproof naming the wildcard-certificate or shared-hosting explanation for a SAN that is not a real host

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers certificate or TLS intelligence. The single db item containing the phrase 'certificate transparency' (1 of 1111) is a dns_enum item about AXFR refusal that mentions CT in passing. The corpus has no CT class, no certificate inventory competency, and no CA/Browser Forum publisher at all. This is the highest-value, lowest-cost gap in the entire registry.

competencies.name: Historical and de-provisioned asset discovery
competencies.produces: historically-served URL and hostname set with first/last-seen timestamps, and the set of names whose current DNS no longer resolves
competencies.contact_rationale: Archive and historical-DNS data is published or pre-collected. No contact with the target is needed to acquire or to reason about it. The reason it matters operationally is the opposite: the point is to find assets the target does NOT currently serve, so contacting them is precisely what you are avoiding.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the Internet Archive's own documentation of its capture and replay guarantees, plus a second independent publisher org, and a disproof naming the evidence that a historical name is still live (a current 200 on the archived path) which would remove it from the stale set

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers historical asset discovery. db substring probe for 'wayback' returns 0 items. Note the seeding difficulty: no standards body publishes a normative specification for web archiving, so this class will have the hardest evidence_standard of any new class and will likely sit at lead tier. That difficulty is itself the finding.

competencies.name: IP, ASN and routing attribution
competencies.produces: IP-to-ASN-to-RIR-to-organisation attribution set with the registry record backing each hop, plus hosted-vs-announced distinction
competencies.contact_rationale: BGP and the address registries publish their data; RDAP responses are queries to a registry, not to the target. Attribution reasoning is pure architecture work over published routing data.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the IANA special-purpose address registry or an RIR's published routing data policy, plus a second independent registry org, and a disproof naming the shared-hosting or CDN announcement that would make an ASN-level attribution a misattribution of the actual operator

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers IP/ASN attribution. db substring probe for 'bgp' returns 0 items. The 9 items containing 'asn' are substring matches inside the words 'reason', 'season' or 'ASN' inside Kerberos and takeover prose, not autonomous-system numbers. There is no IANA or RIR publisher anywhere in the 513-row source table.

competencies.name: Domain registration and RDAP/WHOIS intelligence
competencies.produces: registration record: registrar, creation and expiry dates, nameserver set, registrant organisation, and the historical-registrant delta set
competencies.contact_rationale: RDAP replaced WHOIS partly to make registration data machine-readable and published. A query goes to a registry, not to the target. Fully assessable offline from captured RDAP responses.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the IETF RDAP specification for the query semantics plus ICANN's registration-data policy for what the fields mean, and a disproof naming the privacy-proxy or thin-registry response that would make the registrant field uninformative

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers registration data. db substring probe for 'registrar' / 'whois' / 'rdap' returns no recon-class items. The only registration-adjacent material in the corpus is inside dns_enum and subdomain_takeover as provider de-provisioning prose.

competencies.name: Public repository and source-code intelligence
competencies.produces: organisation-attributed code artifact set: repositories, leaked credentials, infrastructure references in commit history, exposed configuration files
inputs_required: author names derived from other OSINT
competencies.contact_rationale: Public repositories are published material. Mining commit history, searching for credentials, and reading shipped configuration are all document-analysis tasks against data the owner chose to publish. No target contact required at any stage, including the assessment.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the platform's own documentation of its visibility and retention model, plus OWASP for the credential-exposure consequence, and a disproof naming the evidence that a credential is a test/example value rather than a live secret

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers repository intelligence. db substring probe: 21 items mention 'github' and 2 mention 'repository', all as incidental prose inside other classes' items (info_disclosure's coordinated-scraping claim, supply_chain). There is no GitHub or GitLab publisher in the source table. Supply_chain (18 items, all on-topic) is about dependency compromise, not about mining an organisation's own public code.

competencies.name: Organisational and personnel identity attribution
competencies.produces: organisation identity set: legal entity, brand aliases, author handles, email format, role-to-person mapping, and the confidence tier on each attribution
competencies.contact_rationale: Purely published-source inference. The competency is entirely about confidence tiering and false-attribution rejection, which is a reasoning discipline rather than a collection technique.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher stating the attribution method's own reliability limits, plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the same-name-across-organisations collision that would refute an attribution

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers identity attribution. db substring probe: 41 items mention 'email' and 12 mention 'breach', all inside credential_access, info_disclosure or authn as exploitation or authentication claims, none as an OSINT competency.

competencies.name: Email address and mail-surface discovery
competencies.produces: valid address set with per-address verification basis, the organisation's email format rule, and the mail infrastructure record (SPF/DKIM/DMARC posture, MX set)
competencies.contact_rationale: Address sources are published (vendor listings, public commits, press). The mail-authentication posture is published in DNS. The one contact-requiring sub-step, SMTP verification, is explicitly out of scope for this competency and belongs to service_discovery.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the IETF email specifications for SPF/DKIM/DMARC semantics plus a second independent org (M3AAWG), and a disproof naming the catch-all MX pattern that would make address format inference useless for a specific-address claim

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers mail-surface discovery. The 41 items containing 'email' are authentication- or credential-related claims in other classes. Neither M3AAWG nor the email RFCs appear in the source table.

competencies.name: Credential-breach corpus correlation
competencies.produces: correlated credential set with per-record provenance (which corpus, which field, what hashing scheme) and the verification that distinguishes a live credential from an expired one
competencies.contact_rationale: Published breach corpora and public-code secrets are documents. The competency's substance is provenance discipline and false-attribution rejection, both of which are document-analysis reasoning.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher of the corpus's own methodology, plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the reuse-rate and password-rotation evidence that would refute a claim that a leaked credential is still valid

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers breach correlation. 12 items mention 'breach' and all are inside credential_access, authn, info_disclosure or smuggling as claims about credential DUMPING consequences, not about correlating a public corpus against a target's identity set.

competencies.name: Search-index and public-document surface mining
competencies.produces: indexed-asset set for the organisation: URLs, documents, cached snippets, and the query construction that surfaced each
competencies.contact_rationale: Search engines index the public web; querying an index is not contacting the target. Assessment is a query-construction reasoning exercise.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the search engine's own published operator documentation for the syntax and the robots exclusion semantics, plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the stale-index entry whose cached snippet describes a surface the target no longer serves

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers search-index mining. No search-engine publisher appears in the source table. Note: this competency's only sub-skill that touches the target is confirming a candidate URL, which belongs to web_application_discovery.

competencies.name: Cloud tenant and asset discovery
competencies.produces: cloud asset set attributable to the organisation: storage containers, instance roles, serverless functions, managed stores, and the naming convention that predicted each
inputs_required: known cloud account or tenant identifiers
competencies.contact_rationale: The discovery mechanism is naming-convention prediction plus unauthenticated or low-privilege listing against the provider's own API, not against the customer's asset. Where a listing requires the organisation's own credentials, that sub-step is a contact-requiring sub-competency and is out of scope here. Assessment is reasoning over provider naming rules and captured listing output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the Cloud Security Alliance's CCM control for asset inventory plus a second independent org (NIST), and a disproof naming the account-ID or naming-convention break that would make a predicted asset unattributable

coverage.justification: measured: NO cloud class exists. class_domain has no 'cloud' value at all. There is no domains/cloud directory. The 34 items containing 'cloud' and 45 containing 'aws' sit inside ssrf (metadata-service claims), info_disclosure (2 AWS enumeration-attribution items) and credential_access - all exploitation or disclosure claims. No Cloud Security Alliance or NIST publisher appears in the source table.

competencies.name: Cloud storage exposure assessment
competencies.produces: per-container exposure verdict: list permission, object read permission, versioning, and the ACL or bucket-policy clause responsible
competencies.contact_rationale: The permission model is published by the provider; the exposure verdict is reasoning over a container's published policy. An unauthenticated read is a query to the provider endpoint about a public container, not a contact with the customer's infrastructure. Assessment is a policy-reading exercise on captured output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the cloud provider's own authorization documentation for the permission semantics plus a second independent org (CSA or NIST), and a disproof naming the bucket-policy condition that would deny the anonymous read that was otherwise demonstrated

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers cloud storage exposure. db substring probe for 's3 bucket' returns 2 items, both inside host_header and both about HashiCorp Vault, not about cloud object storage permissions.

competencies.name: Cloud identity and permission-surface discovery
competencies.produces: identity and permission graph: principals, roles, trust relationships, cross-account grants, and the specific grant that widens reach
inputs_required: the read-only principal available to the assessment
competencies.contact_rationale: The permission model is published and the graph is a query against the provider's control plane, not against a customer host. Requires the organisation's own read credential to be complete, which is a scope precondition rather than target contact. Assessment is graph reasoning over captured authorization output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the cloud provider's IAM documentation for the grant semantics plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the permission boundary or condition key that would have blocked the assumed escalation

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers cloud identity. The two closest items are in info_disclosure and describe AWS resource-explorer-2 listing and a service-linked-role index that bypasses enumeration ATTRIBUTION. Both are single items in a disclosure class, both are about attribution evasion rather than permission-graph discovery, and neither can carry this competency.

competencies.name: Cross-source infrastructure correlation
competencies.produces: unified asset graph joining DNS names, IP ranges, certificates, cloud assets, AD objects and code artifacts, with each edge carrying its evidence and its confidence
competencies.contact_rationale: Honest answer: the correlation REASONING requires no contact, but a graph built without contact is unvalidated - it will assert edges between assets that were never observed to relate. The competency therefore requires contact to be evidenced, even though its analysis is offline. Assessment is architecture_reasoning over a supplied graph.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher for each edge type's semantics, two independent orgs minimum across the graph, and a disproof naming the shared-hosting or CDN-tenant coincidence that would refute an asserted ownership edge

coverage.justification: measured: 34/54 off-topic across the three contributing classes (dns_enum 14, internal_recon 7, segmentation_analysis 13). Measured compounding: the more classes a cross-cutting competency aggregates, the worse its on-topic ratio, because each class carries its own filler. Four of this competency's inputs (subdomain_discovery, certificate_tls_intelligence, cloud_asset_discovery, and a clean AD object set) are ABSENT or CONTAMINATED, so the graph cannot currently be built from corpus knowledge at all.

competencies.name: Attack-surface prioritisation and hunt ordering
competencies.produces: ranked asset list with the reach, privilege and blast-radius rationale for each rank, and the next competency to invoke for the top asset
competencies.contact_rationale: Prioritisation is a decision procedure over artifacts already collected. It adds no new observation of its own, so it requires no contact. This is the one cross_domain competency that is fully assessable from a supplied graph and the corpus's existing class and chain tables.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher's risk-assessment or attack-tactic taxonomy for the prioritisation criteria, plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the lower-ranked asset whose unlogged access would have outranked the top pick

coverage.justification: measured: NO class performs prioritisation. The 71 chain rows are the corpus's nearest analogue and they are per-class (mostly auto-generated chain.<class>.auto.01), not cross-asset. 42 items contain 'attack surface' but all as prose inside technique claims. Nothing in the corpus ranks recon output against exploitability.

competencies.name: Configuration and hardening recon
competencies.produces: per-surface hardening posture: the setting, the vendor default, the hardened value, and the observable evidence for each
competencies.contact_rationale: A configuration is a fact about a deployed instance. Reading it requires either contact or a captured config artifact. Assessable on captured output.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from the vendor's own hardening documentation for the recommended setting plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the scope or exception that would make the observed setting compliant

coverage.justification: measured: tools/recon_audit_offtopic.py reports 10/13 off-topic (76.9%) for misconfig - the second-worst ratio in the corpus. Only 3 on-topic items, of which two are password-policy lines duplicated verbatim into exposed_rmm and service_enumeration_detail. misconfig is also one of the 22 classes with no class_domain row, so it is not even assigned to a domain.

competencies.name: Recon scope, authorisation and evidence-provenance bounding
competencies.produces: written scope boundary: what may be probed, from which sources, with what rate, and the provenance record for every collected artifact
inputs_required: authorisation statement or explicit research-only constraint
competencies.contact_rationale: This is the competency that DETERMINES whether any other competency may make contact. It is itself entirely a policy and provenance discipline, and is the reason this registry can be honest about the contact boundary at all.
competencies.evidence_standard: verbatim quote from a named publisher's own testing methodology defining the authorisation boundary, plus a second independent org, and a disproof naming the unlogged action that would have breached the boundary

coverage.justification: measured: NO class covers scope bounding. The constraint itself is real and enforced in CODE - CONTROL/rules.md R13 sets config.RESEARCH_ONLY=True and OPERATOR.md states the system does not scan, fuzz, or exploit - but it is a code invariant with no evidence class, no items, and no assessment. A competency whose failure mode is an unauthorised probe, and which has zero assessed items, is the most consequential gap in this registry.

proposed_new_classes.name: Historical and De-provisioned Asset Discovery
proposed_new_classes.why_absent: measured ABSENT: 0 classes, 0 items, 0 for 'wayback'. Archives are how retired subdomains are found, which is the precondition for most takeover findings.
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_a: Internet Archive - publishes its own capture, replay and index guarantees, which is the authority for what an archived record can prove
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_b: Library of Congress - an independent archive publisher with a different preservation mandate and publication model

proposed_new_classes.name: Passive DNS and Historical Resolution Intelligence
proposed_new_classes.why_absent: measured ABSENT: 0 classes, 0 items. Passive DNS is the mechanism that turns a single IP into a name set with history, and it is entirely a published-data discipline.
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_a: IETF (RFC 8499, DNS Terminology) - the normative definition of the record types a passive dataset reports
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_b: CISA - publishes guidance on DNS-layer visibility and on the abuse of DNS infrastructure, from a government body independent of IETF

proposed_new_classes.name: IP, ASN and Routing Attribution
proposed_new_classes.why_absent: measured ABSENT: 0 classes, 0 items, 0 for 'bgp'. The 9 'asn' substring hits are inside 'reason'/'season' in Kerberos and takeover prose. No IANA or RIR publisher exists in the 513-row source table.
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_a: IANA - publishes the authoritative IP special-purpose address registry and the autonomous-system number registry
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_b: RIPE NCC - an independent Regional Internet Registry publishing its own routing and whois data policy, and a different organisation from IANA
proposed_new_classes.note: ORG-level and the cleanest seed pair in the entire proposal: IANA and RIPE NCC are unambiguously two organisations, and both publish normative, quotable registry data. Do not substitute another RIR for the second seed without recording why. URLs unverified.

proposed_new_classes.name: Domain Registration and RDAP/WHOIS Intelligence
proposed_new_classes.why_absent: measured ABSENT: 0 classes, 0 items. Nameserver sets from registration data seed every DNS-based competency, and RDAP made the data machine-readable precisely for this use.
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_a: IETF (RFC 7480 series, RDAP) - normative for the query and response semantics
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_b: ICANN - the policy authority for what registration data means and how it is exposed, independent of the IETF spec
proposed_new_classes.note: ORG-level. Do NOT seed from a registrar's own marketing page; that is a single vendor describing its own product, which is the exact R1 failure mode. URLs unverified.

proposed_new_classes.name: Public Repository and Source-Code Intelligence
proposed_new_classes.why_absent: measured ABSENT: 0 classes, 0 items. The 21 'github' items are incidental prose inside other classes. Leaked credentials and infrastructure references in an organisation's own public code are a first-class recon source with no class behind them.
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_a: GitHub (docs) - the authoritative publisher of its own visibility, retention and secret-scanning model, which is the capability being reasoned about
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_b: GitLab - a genuinely different organisation with a different default-visibility and retention model, so the two do not collapse under publisher_org
proposed_new_classes.note: ORG-level. Both seeds are vendor self-documentation and both are R20 tier-'lead' by construction; this class will need a third, non-vendor normative org (e.g. OWASP on secret handling) to reach a genuine normative two-publisher gate. Stated here so the promotion blocker is designed in, not discovered. URLs unverified.

proposed_new_classes.seed_org_b: MITRE - publishes the recon and discovery tactic taxonomy that names the source types a pivot should move between

proposed_new_classes.seed_org_a: Cloud Security Alliance - publishes the CCM control set that defines what a complete cloud asset inventory must contain, from a body that is neither a cloud vendor nor a general standards body
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_b: NIST - publishes cloud configuration security guidance from a government body independent of both the CSA and the vendors

proposed_new_classes.name: Cloud Identity and Permission-Surface Discovery
proposed_new_classes.why_absent: measured ABSENT: 0 classes. The two closest items sit in info_disclosure and concern enumeration ATTRIBUTION evasion via resource-explorer-2 and a service-linked-role index - a different observable with a different disproof.
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_a: Cloud Security Alliance - publishes the identity and access-management control set the discovery is scored against
proposed_new_classes.seed_org_b: NIST - publishes cloud identity and authorisation guidance independent of the CSA and of any vendor

proposed_new_classes.why_absent: measured ABSENT: 0 classes, 0 items. open_questions: The task brief states 1111 item rows; the db holds 1112 item rows of which 1111 are status='active' and 1 is 'superseded'. Every count in this registry is the ACTIVE count, so it reconciles with both wks.cli metrics (items_total 1111) and the raw row count (1112). No reconciliation problem, but the two numbers should not be cited interchangeably.

recon_audit_offtopic.py probes only 23 of the 62 classes. Its VOCAB map has no entry for ad_ldap, ad_acl_abuse, ad_kerberos, ad_ntlm, ad_delegation, ad_group_policy, ad_trust_abuse, adcs_abuse, credential_access, pass_the_hash, password_attacks, lateral_movement, tunneling_pivoting, and most web classes. For those, on_topic() returns True unconditionally, so a 0.0% off-topic figure means NOT PROBED, not clean. I have reported ad_ldap, ad_kerberos, ad_trust_abuse and ad_group_policy as EVIDENCED on the strength of their 21/21, 13/13, 14/14 and 13/13 active item counts and their real chains, not on the probe. The probe's silence on those four classes is an unverified-clean claim, not a verified-clean one, and the probe should be extended before the EVIDENCED verdicts are relied on.

The probe is vocabulary matching, not judgement. A false NEGATIVE is guaranteed for any class whose correct vocabulary is absent from its list. rdp is listed with vocabulary ['rdp','remote desktop','nla','credssp','clipboard','port 3389'] and returns 0/15 off-topic, which is credible because those words are narrow. subdomain_takeover likewise. But exposed_rmm's 82.6% could be partly probe error in the other direction and the 4 surviving items were not individually read by me - I read dns_enum's generated SKILL.md, which independently confirmed its contamination, and I did not read the other classes' pages.

CONTROL/OPERATOR.md names 9 network classes that could never promote because their seeds sat on attack.mitre.org + cwe.mitre.org, which collapse to one MITRE org: ad_ntlm, ad_delegation, credential_access, lateral_movement, pass_the_hash, password_attacks, segmentation_analysis, service_enumeration, tunneling_pivoting. I measured the CURRENT seed sets in wks.network_taxonomy._NET_SEED and found all 24 network classes now carry >= 2 distinct publisher orgs, with no thin seeds. I do not know when or by what the re-seeding happened, and whether verify-seeds has been run since. That is a drift question I cannot answer read-only.

python -m wks.seed --help does NOT print help: it executes the seeder. I ran it once. It reported 'registered 40 classes (0 new)'. I diffed db/wks.db against db/wks-pre-resynth-20261002-205254.db across bug_class, item, chain, fp_case, source, quality, item_source, run and event: every count identical, 0 new classes, 0 new items. No mutation. The parent operator should know the CLI is un-safe to probe with --help.

wks.cli gaps prints an 'fp' column whose value does not match the fp_case row count (dns_enum: gaps says 2, fp_case has 0). OPERATOR.md already explains this - the column counts fp_rule items, and MATURITY_MIN_FP_RULES counts fp_case ROWS. Every fp_cases figure in this registry is a direct fp_case table count, so this registry and `wks.cli gaps` will disagree on fp figures by design. Worth aligning the column name before anyone reconciles the two by eye.

22 of 62 classes have NO class_domain row at all, including three recon-relevant ones: info_disclosure, misconfig, subdomain_takeover. R27 says a class with no gated items should render as a map, but these three have 13, 15 and 14 items respectively and are simultaneously unassigned to a domain. I could not determine whether the missing row is a defect or a deliberate 'unclassified' state.

I could not verify a single URL in this cycle: no web search and no web fetch were run, per the mission constraint. EVERY publisher org named in proposed_new_classes is named from prior knowledge and every corresponding URL is marked unverified. They must be resolved through db/sources.json and GET-verified before any of these classes is seeded - OPERATOR.md records that 34% of first-pass learn.microsoft.com guesses were 404.

The requires_target_contact split is my judgement, not a measurement. The one place I am least confident is infrastructure_correlation, which I marked true because an uncontacted correlation graph would assert unverified ownership edges, while its analysis is entirely offline. A reviewer could defensibly mark it false on the grounds that the competency adds no observation. I chose true to keep the honesty burden on the graph.

cloud_asset_discovery, cloud_storage_exposure and cloud_identity_discovery are all marked false. If the organisation's own cloud credentials are required for completeness, those become contact-requiring sub-steps against a customer estate. The scope precondition versus target-contact distinction I applied is defensible but is not a rule that exists anywhere in CONTROL/rules.md today, and it probably should.

I did not measure whether the 71 chain rows are substantively useful. Most are chain.<class>.auto.01, and spot-checking chain 49 (dns_enum) showed three generic steps - 'Establish the precondition and record the baseline' / 'Exercise it against the target and capture the raw' / 'Confirm the result reproduces and crosses the bound' - that name no technique. I counted chain existence per class because that is what MATURITY_MIN_CHAINS=1 measures, but a chain of generic steps satisfies the counter while teaching nothing. The 26 named chains are a different and much better artifact.
